text:
maya: FYI support escalation from Cust-ACCT123 — they report p99 API latency jumping from ~150ms to ~3.2s for traffic from APAC since ~02:00 UTC. Customer provided request ids req_abc123, req_abc124. @ryan can you triage?

ryan: on it. any repro steps or client-side traces?

maya: they sent a client-side trace and a curl timing. quote: "most requests succeed but TLS handshake and first byte are delayed when traffic routes to ap-southeast1-b". attaching their traceroute snippet: 
```
traceroute to api.redwood.example (203.0.113.45), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.0.0.1  1.0 ms  0.9 ms  1.1 ms
 7  198.51.100.2  18.3 ms  19.0 ms  18.7 ms
10  203.0.113.45  520.4 ms  521.0 ms  519.8 ms
```

anita: pulling edge egress logs for ap-southeast POPs. quick look shows GSLB weight rebalance around 01:58 UTC — appears to have shifted a chunk of healthy traffic onto pop "b".

dmitri: running active probes to that client IP from our ap-southeast PoPs. sample probe output: 
```
$ curl -w "%{time_namelookup} %{time_connect} %{time_appconnect} %{time_starttransfer} %{time_total}\n" -o /dev/null -s https://api.redwood.example/health
0.012 0.042 0.512 0.520 0.523
```
appconnect (TLS handshake) ~512ms from pop b, ~20ms from pops a/c.

ryan: ops-bot, can you run p95/p99 probes across ap-southeast PoPs to that client ASN?

ops-bot: probe summary (last 15m): ap-southeast1-a p95=110ms p99=210ms; ap-southeast1-b p95=540ms p99=950ms; ap-southeast1-c p95=130ms p99=240ms.

anita: looks like ap-southeast1-b egress path to that ASN has elevated RTT + occasional loss -> likely peering or transit congestion. opening ticket with our carrier.

dmitri: short-term mitigation suggestion: reduce GSLB weight for ap-southeast1-b to steer traffic away while provider investigates. I can roll back weights now. command: 
```
# rollback weight for pop b to 0.2 (20%)
gslbctl set-weight pop ap-southeast1-b 0.2 --reason "emergency rollback due to egress latency"
```

ryan: please also bump health-check sensitivity for that POP so we avoid routing new long-lived sessions there until stable.

dmitri: initiating rollback -> applied, propagation ~60s.

maya: told customer we are steering away from the affected POP. they reported p99 dropped to ~220ms after ~3 minutes. customer wants postmortem and SLO credit evaluation.

ryan: next steps: 1) keep reduced weight until carrier confirms, 2) correlate GSLB rollout change with our deployment logs (did we push weights/strategy at ~01:58?), 3) collect tcpdump+tls metrics for the affected POP, 4) propose long-term: ASN-specific route steering or prefer peering fallback.

anita: I found a config change in the GSLB config repo merged 01:55 UTC that adjusted weights for ap-southeast region (PR #789). tagging the author for follow-up.

dmitri: carrier ticket opened (CARRIER-5021) referencing packet loss and increased egress latency for our ASN from ap-southeast1-b. I requested expedited peering check.

maya: Customer acknowledged mitigation and will monitor — keeping open as high-priority. they asked for timeline on root cause and permanent fix.

ryan: I will own the postmortem. initial RCA draft: GSLB weight change + transit/peering degradation -> cross-zone route inflation -> TLS handshake tail spike -> p99 latency regression. Mitigations: rollback weights, add more granular health checks, implement ASN-aware GSLB steering, and add egress path alerting.

maya: thanks team. I'll coordinate SLO credit conversation with CS once postmortem is ready. :thumbsup:

anita: added follow-up items to infra board and assigned to carrier/peering.

ryan: closing triage thread, will share postmortem link when ready.
